own_solution.law: Along the incline, ma = mg sin(30°) - μk mg cos(30°), giving a = 3.62694266 m/s². From rest, v² = 2as, so v = sqrt(2 × 3.62694266 × 4) = 5.38661 m/s.
assumptions: The incline is fixed and uniform.
The block slides without rolling, with constant kinetic friction coefficient 0.15.
In the base problem, the stated 4 m begins at release from rest.

T8A07.regime: Spontaneous sliding from rest occurs when μs < tan(30°) ≈ 0.57735. The supplied value 0.35 satisfies this condition; subsequent sliding uses kinetic friction.

T0B87.regime: Spontaneous sliding from rest occurs when μs < tan(30°) ≈ 0.57735. The supplied value 0.35 satisfies this condition; subsequent sliding uses kinetic friction.

notes: Mass cancels between gravitational force, friction and inertia. T3451 and T386C explicitly place an additional uninterrupted 2 m of sliding before the stated 4 m, giving 6 m total from release and v = sqrt(2a × 6). Earlier motion on the bench or floor has no effect after the block is placed on the incline and released from rest. All mass statements specify 2 kg, all static-friction statements specify the dimensionless value 0.35, and all earlier-distance statements specify 2 m. The wooden/solid description supplies no additional dependency under the stated sliding model. The unrelated historical motion is somewhat artificial.
